verses.text: Trouble is coming for those who go down to Egypt for help. They lean on horses and trust in chariots because there are so many and in riders because they’re so strong. They never look to the Holy One of Israel or seek the LORD.
But he’s wise too. He’ll bring disaster and won’t take back what he said. He’ll rise up against the household of evildoers and against anyone who helps those who do wrong.

Egyptians are human. They aren’t God. Their horses are flesh and blood, with no power of spirit. When the LORD stretches out his hand, the helper will stumble, the one getting help will fall, and they’ll both be wiped out together.

The LORD told me, “Think of a lion or a young lion growling over its prey. Get a whole crowd of shepherds shouting at it, and their voices won’t scare it or make it back down. That’s how the LORD of Armies will come down to fight on Mount Zion and its heights.
Like birds hovering overhead, the LORD of Armies will guard Jerusalem. He’ll protect and rescue it. He’ll pass over it and keep it safe.”
Children of Israel, come back to the one you’ve rebelled against so deeply.
That day everyone will throw away their silver and gold idols, the sin their own hands made.
“The Assyrian will fall by a sword no human swings. A sword from no human hand will devour him. He’ll run from the sword, and his young men will be forced to work.
His rock will give way in terror, and his officers will panic at the sight of the banner,” says the LORD, whose fire burns in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
